description: In this 300-level seminar, students will study key criminal cases from the 20th century to explore the connection between true crime, copaganda, and the expansion of the prison industrial complex. Students will use a race, gender, and capital lens to examine the cases of Adam Walsh, O.J. Simpson, the New Jersey Four, the DC Sniper case, and more. As part of the class, students will also conduct an independent research project that examines the historiography of contemporary crime and punishment in the U.S. Using a variety of sources including court transcripts, art, and documentary film, students will learn how to identify and examine key trends within this historiography and the relationship between true crime and the expansion of the carceral state. Prerequisite: HIST 199 is recommended but not required.
